_meta.que_es: Traducción de referencia de las 70 preguntas del gold set, para medir la calidad de la traducción automática que hace Nova en producción (P3).
_meta.por_que_otro_traductor: El traductor de producción es Nova. Medir a Nova con Nova es A == A, el error que la auditoría adversarial ya encontró una vez en este repo.
_meta.regla_1: Se traduce DESDE EL ESPAÑOL. No se copia ninguna frase del span esperado: eso metería el gold set dentro del instrumento y el recall subiría por filtración, no por calidad.
_meta.regla_2: Un término del dominio se traduce por su equivalente canónico en inglés cuando el español ya lo dice (exhaustividad → recall), no cuando hay que adivinarlo.
_meta.sesgo_declarado: Quien escribió estas referencias había visto los primeros 110 caracteres de cada span al auditar el cache. La regla 1 acota el daño pero no lo elimina: por eso el veredicto de P3 se apoya en la CLASIFICACIÓN de los defectos, que es verificable leyendo, y no sólo en el delta de recall.
_meta.que_califica_clase: `clase` NO describe esta traducción de referencia: describe el defecto de la traducción que hizo NOVA para esa misma pregunta, juzgada contra esta referencia. `ok` significa que la de Nova está bien.

clasificacion.torpe: calco o construcción rara, pero el sentido y los términos se conservan
clasificacion.termino: un término del dominio se perdió o se tradujo por uno no canónico
clasificacion.sentido: la traducción dice otra cosa que el original

q-00-01.en: How do human recruiters adapt their criteria depending on the type of company, and where do language models have to infer this preference from?

q-00-02.en: How many objectives does the study set out, and what is the first one?

q-00-03.en: What was done so that the variation across evaluations would not come from how the task was presented?

q-00-04.en: What ethical safeguards were taken with the resumes and with the human experts who took part?

q-00-05.en: What does the study recommend organizations do with job descriptions and with human oversight?

q-00-06.en: Which theory does the study contribute to, and in what way?

q-02-01.en: Why does an error made by an algorithmic system weigh differently on a streaming platform than in a hiring process?

q-02-02.en: In how many ways does the paper say it contributes to the literature?

q-02-03.en: What distinction do the authors draw when mapping ethical considerations?

q-02-04.en: When did the GDPR come into effect, and how does the paper characterize it relative to other regulations?

q-02-05.en: Did the review find any article analyzing AI recruiting from an established ethical theory?

q-02-06.en: From which perspectives is the topic addressed in the reviewed literature?

q-03-01.en: What does integrating RAG into the system let recruiters adjust dynamically?

q-03-02.en: What is the responsibility of the resume evaluator agent within the multi-agent framework?

q-03-03.en: What does each of the summarizer's three sub-agents assess?

q-03-04.en: What does the Spearman correlation measure in the system evaluation, and how does it differ from Pearson's?

q-03-05.en: What do recruiters receive under a single-model approach versus the proposed modular approach?

q-03-06.en: Can the system assess resumes against company-specific scoring criteria without retraining the model?

q-05-01.en: What problems does manual resume screening introduce besides the time it demands?

q-05-02.en: How large was the dataset the system was evaluated on?

q-05-03.en: What normalization steps does the system apply after extracting the text?

q-05-04.en: How are the weights of each matching attribute determined?

q-05-05.en: What does Smart-Hiring provide that systems computing only embedding similarity do not?

q-05-06.en: What does the system's explainability layer contribute according to the conclusions?

q-08-01.en: What was the performance of the language models benchmarked against in the experiment?

q-08-02.en: How are resumes arriving in different formats standardized before being processed?

q-08-03.en: Why does feeding a sentence into the model not guarantee it returns the expected label?

q-08-04.en: Into how many distinct processes is the final candidate evaluation stage divided?

q-08-05.en: In what respect does the agent significantly surpass traditional manual screening?

q-17-01.en: Which two RAG-building frameworks does the tool integrate with?

q-17-02.en: Does the answer relevance metric take factuality into account?

q-17-03.en: What does the context relevance metric specifically penalise?

q-17-04.en: Why can two runs of the same experiment with the same configuration give different results?

q-17-05.en: Which provider do the library's metrics use by default?

q-17-06.en: Which kind of models do the authors recommend prioritizing when choosing the judge?

q-19-01.en: When does training of the system's judges stop?

q-19-02.en: What does the method use the human preference validation set for?

q-19-03.en: What are the lightweight judges proposed by the framework fine-tuned on?

q-19-04.en: What advantage comes from being able to evaluate each component separately?

q-20-01.en: What conceptual role does retrieval play with respect to the model's attention?

q-20-02.en: What assumption does the method that routes queries by self-reflection rest on?

q-20-03.en: How did the authors determine the reasons why retrieval was failing?

q-20-04.en: Why is a query requiring multi-step reasoning hard for the retriever?

q-20-05.en: When does retrieval remain preferable even though long context performs better?

q-20-06.en: What is the model told to write when the question cannot be answered from the passages?

q-22-01.en: What is obtained by comparing the retrieved spans against the reference spans?

q-22-02.en: How is recall defined in this study, and why was that metric chosen?

q-22-03.en: What is the primary purpose of the generation metrics according to the authors?

q-22-04.en: Why is it not sufficient that a metric correlates well with human judgment to trust it?

q-22-05.en: What is the risk of integrating too many systems into the correlation study?

q-24-01.en: By how much can the number of biased outcomes increase when a document is shortened?

q-24-02.en: Why is research using job descriptions taken from the web hard to reproduce?

q-24-03.en: Which statistical test is used to decide whether a group is overrepresented among those selected?

q-24-04.en: What was compared to verify that the document retrieval approach was suitable for screening?

q-24-05.en: Which race and gender groups was the analysis limited to?

q-24-06.en: What tension must researchers working on documents that carry identity signals resolve?

q-25-01.en: How were the confidence intervals for the race gap computed, and over how many clusters?

q-25-02.en: How many resume pairs per model were used in the gender audit?

q-27-01.en: What is the main research gap the review identifies?

q-27-02.en: What does data profiling aim to discover, and what does it give the company?

q-27-03.en: What example do they give of a variable that predicts tenure but discriminates if used for hiring?

q-27-04.en: Which aspect of algorithmic decision-making has found little attention compared with its organizational advantages?

q-27-05.en: Why is implicit discrimination more problematic than apparent discrimination?

q-27-06.en: What do the authors recommend about relying entirely on the algorithm for the decision?

q-35-01.en: How is the job-candidate matching task formalized?

q-35-02.en: What advantage does the cross-domain approach have for training the defense?

q-35-03.en: What is the first measure of the defense-in-depth scheme they propose?

q-35-04.en: How should the task instruction be separated from the candidate data?

q-35-05.en: How do these attacks differ from a classic jailbreak?

q-35-06.en: Which factors should be treated as secondary unless the job description states otherwise?
